title: Docs, comments, changelog, and provenance audit of the entire repository surface
team_configuration: 1 (standard 4-agent graph: A1 Boundary Engineer -> A2 Red-Team Verifier (Failure Hunter) -> A3 Release Warden -> A4 Docs Scribe). A4's role here is narrower than usual: the audit itself is doc-shaped, so A4 runs only if A1's candidate leaves CHANGELOG.md/[Unreleased] or .agent/README.md status lines stale for THIS audit's own change -- otherwise A4 writes a SKIPPED receipt, per its own procedure.
objective: The repository's prose surface (docs, READMEs, code comments, CHANGELOG, audit/performance narratives) has accumulated claims across many phases and PRs, and its provenance surface (which claims trace to which code, tests, and results artifacts) has never been audited as a coherent whole. Concrete trigger: PRs #112-#116 (five security fixes) merged into main after 0.6.1, and CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] section is still empty -- a provenance break between git history and the changelog. This directive authorizes a full docs/comments/changelog/provenance audit: read every prose surface line by line, verify every falsifiable claim it makes against the actual code/tests/results it cites, fix what is wrong or stale (docs-only and comment-only changes), and produce a provenance ledger mapping each surviving claim to its evidence. Claims that cannot be traced to evidence must be corrected or removed, not left standing.
base_sha_note: Tip of main after PR #116 merged (2026-09-06). Re-verify with `git rev-parse main` before starting A1_WRITE if time has passed; if main has moved, restate the audit against the new tip.
scope: Every Markdown prose surface, read line by line: README.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, PERFORMANCE.md, PHASE3_PERFORMANCE_ANALYSIS.md, AUDIT.md, FINDINGS-INBOX.md, docs/BENCHMARK.md, docs/DEMO.md, docs/MONITOR.md, docs/THREAT-COVERAGE.md, demo/README.md, red-team/README.md, packages/fw-agent/README.md, and CHANGELOG.md.

The doc gap: packages/fw-control/ has no README.md at all. Either add one that makes only evidence-traceable claims, or record a receipt-level finding explaining why none is warranted. (packages/fw-control/README.md is inside A4's DOC_PATH_ALLOWLIST and is ordinary prose, so A1 creating it is in-bounds.)

Code comments in the enforcement path, audited as CLAIMS, not read past: packages/fw-agent/index.js, packages/fw-agent/sync-worker.js, every file under packages/fw-agent/src/ (including the comments newly added by PR #116 in src/aho-corasick.js -- verify the aliasing example arithmetic and the 'keyword-unreachable bucket' invariant still match the code), packages/fw-control/src/server.js, and scripts/*.js. Every comment that asserts behavior ('Node routes .json through its own handler', 'this is O(N)', 'fail-closed by default') must be checked against the code it describes and the test that proves it; stale, wrong, or untraceable comments get corrected or deleted.

CHANGELOG.md provenance: reconstruct what SHOULD be in [Unreleased] from git history since the 0.6.1 tag-equivalent state (PRs #112, #113, #114, #115, #116 at minimum -- verify the actual merge list with `git log` rather than trusting this enumeration), and reconcile: either write the missing entries (each claim traceable to a merged-PR fact) or document why the section was intentionally left empty.

Claim-to-artifact provenance spot-checks: numbers and verdicts quoted in docs (benchmark figures in docs/BENCHMARK.md and PERFORMANCE.md, red-team detection rates, coverage percentages, the execution-surface matrix classification in docs/THREAT-COVERAGE.md) must trace to a committed artifact under results/ that actually contains that number/verdict -- recompute or cite; any number that no artifact supports gets corrected or marked stale.

Cross-surface consistency: the same fact stated in two places (e.g. known-bypass lists in docs/THREAT-COVERAGE.md vs red-team/README.md vs what `npm run redteam` actually prints; the self-integrity file list described in prose vs the 4 lockstep code locations) must agree. Disagreements are findings.
out_of_scope: Changing any runtime behavior. This audit may edit prose and comments ONLY. The one exception-free hard line: no logic, signature, ordering, or constant changes in any .js file. If a comment is wrong because the CODE is wrong, the code defect is reported as a finding with file/line and evidence -- never fixed under this directive (same discipline as PENTEST-006/007's audit-only lanes).
Version bumps, release tagging, CHANGELOG version-heading creation or dating beyond the [Unreleased] section -- a human release decision, per .agent/rules/security-gates.md.

.agent/ control-plane files (contracts, scripts, rules, agents) -- forbidden paths for A1 by the graph's own rule; prose ABOUT the graph in .agent/README.md / .agent/RUNBOOK.md is in scope for the audit's verification pass but any corrections to those two files ride A4's allowlist discipline.
Re-running or re-litigating PENTEST-006/007's security findings -- this audit verifies that PROSE about those findings is accurate; it does not re-adjudicate the findings.
Third-party dependency documentation, npm registry/page metadata, and the npm Trusted Publishing workflow.
success_criteria: engineer-receipt.json honestly enumerates every prose surface read (file by file, no sampling), every claim checked, every correction made in changed_files, and every code-defect finding deferred rather than fixed -- with a real test/evidence run proving the docs-only candidate changes nothing executable.

changed_files contains ONLY prose/comment edits (Markdown, and comment-text-only hunks inside .js files). A2 independently confirms every .js hunk in the candidate diff is comment-only -- any executable-token change is an automatic verifier FAIL, no judgment call.

If any self-integrity-listed file's comments were edited, the candidate includes the regenerated packages/fw-agent/.helios-baseline and the engineer receipt cites the `npm run baseline` / `npm run baseline:check` evidence -- release-warden.js's recomputation carve-out must excuse it, which is only possible if the regeneration is mathematically exact.

CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] accurately reflects the post-0.6.1 merges (#112-#116) with no claim that cannot be traced to a merged PR, or the engineer receipt documents a deliberate, evidence-backed decision to leave it empty.

The provenance ledger (a new docs/ or results/ artifact, or a receipt section -- engineer's choice, documented) maps every surviving quantitative/verdict claim in the audited prose to the results/ artifact or test that supports it, and shows zero unsupported numbers remaining.

Failure Hunter (A2) independently re-derives a sample of at least 10 corrected claims from the raw artifacts (not from A1's narrative) and finds no false or unverifiable claim remaining in the candidate; A2 also confirms no false positive was introduced (a correct claim deleted or weakened without cause).
no P0 regression; the full regression matrix (npm run test:unit / test:adversarial / test:integration / test:auth / test:matrix / baseline:check) passes on the candidate unchanged
candidate SHA remains immutable during verification; evidence bundle complete

release-warden.js runs unmodified and its verdict is reported verbatim by A3. Note for A3's report: this directive touches only prose/comments, so sync_required should come back false UNLESS a self-integrity or detector-relevant file's comments were edited (index.js, detector.js, behavior-tracker.js, aho-corasick.js, ast-scan.js, policy.js) -- in which case sync_required=true is the honest, expected mechanical answer and must not be argued down.
